title: ctxroute — configuration
description: GLOBAL config of the framework (maintainer decision 17/07/2026: the JSON does ONLY global — per-doc cadence lives in the doc's frontmatter, never here. Zero duplication between the two). Cascade: doc frontmatter > global defaults here.

cadence.description: Cadence settings — SAME vocabulary as an entry (anti-synonym law: one concept = one word, whatever the stage). All keys optional.

note.description: AUTHOR COMMENT — never read by the engine. Here: 'why this default for this WHOLE category'. ⚠️ ADDED on 05/08/2026 by the vocabulary-symmetry gate, which found the gap on its first run: `note` existed in file docs, MCP docs and skill entries, but NOT in `defaults.{source}` — an omission, not a decision. Symmetry is the DEFAULT; every exception must be justified in writing.

enforce.description: REFUSE the action instead of informing (05/08/2026). ⚠️ Only meaningful for a category whose docs are ALL in `mode: once` — the engine honors `enforce` only on an EFFECTIVE `once` mode (anti-loop guarantee in gate.js), otherwise it informs. Setting `enforce` on a whole category is DISCOURAGED: every first action of a session would be refused, and a system people endure ends up unplugged. Reserved for irreversible actions, doc by doc. An entry can opt out with `enforce: false`.

category.description: WHO receives the doc — the language's one word for the acting context (a behavior key, NOT a trigger — same family as `enforce`). It reads the categories a policy DECLARED plus the identity ctxroute DERIVES per gesture: `role:main`, `role:subagent`, `type:<agent type>` (reserved namespaces, never declarable). Flat list = OR; grouped list [[...],[...]] = AND of groups (never both forms mixed); a leading `-` SUBTRACTS (`["role:subagent", "-type:Explore"]` = sub-agents except Explore). Fail-closed: an unmet positive excludes, and so does a negative on an identity the harness did not deliver. `depth:` is refused (no harness names a sub-agent's parent). Absent = no restriction, unchanged since before this key existed (parity). NO global stage, same reasoning as `enforce`: a global `category` would restrict the first gesture of every session on every doc of the fleet.

response.description: Narrow the doc to the moment AFTER the tool answered, and to the answers its `scope`/`exclude` accept (23/09/2026). Written on ONE line as inline JSON, e.g. {"scope": ["posted"]}. It reads every text of the answer at any depth (a JSON text is read as the structure it encodes, key names never match) with the SAME semantics as the gesture's filters: `scope` = OR (flat) or AND of ORs (grouped), `exclude` = none of these may appear. A word of the LANGUAGE, never a parameter name: it is not reached through `keys`, so a tool parameter called `response` can never collide with it. Absent = decided BEFORE the action, exactly as before this key existed (parity). NO global stage: a global value would move every doc of the fleet after the action. Incompatible with `enforce: true`: an action that already ran cannot be refused, and an answer is content no one controls.

filterMode.description: PER-TARGET FILTER, for THIS doc category (52, 15/08/2026) — SAME words, same meaning as the global one. A `"none"` declared here UNSUBSCRIBES the category from a global filter (mirror of the explicit `enforce: false` — without it the stage could not be opted out of). The filterMode+filterList pair cascades TOGETHER: the stage that provides the mode provides its list.

filterList.description: TARGETS of this category's filterMode: MCP server, exact tool name, or wildcard "*" (52, 15/08/2026).

scope.description: PER-SOURCE DEFAULT for the `scope` operator (20/08/2026). An entry that declares it WINS entirely (no merge) — 4-stage cascade, identical to the behaviour keys. Born of a MEASURED defect: making every doc of a category stop reading an observable required writing it on 300+ entries, i.e. an ENUMERATION, born stale. `match` is DELIBERATELY absent from this tier: it is the only operator that CREATES an injection, so a category-wide default would fabricate rules for docs that declare none. Filters can only ever narrow. Original shape: FLAT FORM = OR (inherited, untouched) - GROUPED FORM = AND of ORs (㊺①, 14/08/2026): [["a"],["b"]] = a AND b, [["a","b"],["c"]] = (a OR b) AND c. EXACT MIRROR of frontmatter.js::formeScopeErreur - two form declarations th

exclude.description: PER-SOURCE DEFAULT for the `exclude` operator (20/08/2026). An entry that declares it WINS entirely (no merge) — 4-stage cascade, identical to the behaviour keys. Born of a MEASURED defect: making every doc of a category stop reading an observable required writing it on 300+ entries, i.e. an ENUMERATION, born stale. `match` is DELIBERATELY absent from this tier: it is the only operator that CREATES an injection, so a category-wide default would fabricate rules for docs that declare none. Filters can only ever narrow. Original shape: Patterns to reject (matched on the current path/command) — homonyms (node_modules, dist...).

keys.description: PER-SOURCE DEFAULT for the `keys` operator (20/08/2026). An entry that declares it WINS entirely (no merge) — 4-stage cascade, identical to the behaviour keys. Born of a MEASURED defect: making every doc of a category stop reading an observable required writing it on 300+ entries, i.e. an ENUMERATION, born stale. `match` is DELIBERATELY absent from this tier: it is the only operator that CREATES an injection, so a category-wide default would fabricate rules for docs that declare none. Filters can only ever narrow. Original shape: WHICH parameter keys this entry may see. Flat list = the same universe for the three axes; object = one universe PER axis (match/scope/exclude). A name prefixed with '-' REMOVES the key from the default universe (blackli

enabled.description: GLOBAL switch — false cuts EVERYTHING (injection AND tracking). Distinct from showNotification.

showNotification.description: Controls ONLY the visual 📄 badge — false hides the badge, the real injection continues.

mode.description: dumb = re-injects on every call (debug only, never in a shipped config — gated). once = 1st call then silence until compaction. smart = once + re-injection after N calls to other tools.

defaultThreshold.description: The N of smart mode: number of calls to OTHER tools before re-injection.

defaultDriftUnit.description: GLOBAL unit of the smart counter (18/07/2026): tool = tool calls (framework default, historical behavior); turn = conversation turns (counter fed by turn-count.js on UserPromptSubmit). Cascade: entry driftUnit (doc frontmatter / skill entry) > defaultDriftUnit > framework default 'tool'. Degenerate outside smart (dumb=0, once=∞).

budgetInjection.description: Emission budget of one injection, in CHARACTERS (31/07/2026). Every harness bounds the size of an injection and FILES the overflow away without telling the producer — the agent then receives an intro while believing it holds the whole contract. This budget keeps the output under that wall: whatever does not fit is ANNOUNCED (name + path), never silently lost. Cascade: framework default (budget.js) > harness limit declared by the shell > this key. ⚠️ This key can only REDUCE the budget (Math.min): the harness limit is physical, exceeding it would restore silent truncation at the very moment you think you are loosening the constraint.

stateDir.description: ABSOLUTE path of the directory holding the framework MUTABLE STATE (2026-08-24). OPTIONAL: with the key ABSENT, the state stays exactly where it has always been, the code-derived <repo>/state — zero default change, that is the acceptance criterion of this key, not a preference. ⚠️ WHY IT EXISTS: the state address used to be DERIVED from the CODE address (path.join(__dirname, '..', 'state')), so a SECOND copy of the code was a SECOND state — a SPLIT BRAIN, and this project refuses that class outright because it fails in SILENCE (a `once` document delivered twice, a refusal that forgets itself, nothing red anywhere). Declaring the state address is what will one day let production run from a FROZEN copy of the code while every copy keeps addressing ONE memory. 🛑 A RELATIVE path is a NAMED REFUSAL naming the key and the value, never a silent resolution: a hook is spawned by the harness from wherever the agent happens to stand, so the base directory is not ours to guess and two callers would silently address two different states. An invalid value refuses the same way — never a quiet fallback to the code-derived path, which would let the operator believe the state lives where they wrote it. ⚠️  `CTXROUTE_STATE_DIR` STILL WINS over this key and that order is not negotiable: the variable is RESERVED for tests and doctor.js, it is how every suite isolates itself in a throwaway tmpdir, and a config beating it would make those suites write into the REAL state.

docsDir.description: ABSOLUTE path of the directory holding the MCP DOCS corpus (docs/mcp/*.md) (2026-08-24). OPTIONAL: with the key ABSENT, the corpus stays exactly where it has always been, the code-derived <repo>/docs/mcp — zero default change, that is the acceptance criterion of this key, not a preference. ⚠️ WHY IT EXISTS: this address used to be DERIVED from the CODE address, so FREEZING the code — the cure for the daemon exiting on its own source change at every delivery — would have FROZEN the corpus with it, and the maintainer's doc edits would simply have stopped reaching production, with nothing red anywhere. The engine and the knowledge it delivers are two different questions and must have two different addresses. 🛑 A RELATIVE path is a NAMED REFUSAL naming the key and the value, never a silent resolution: a hook is spawned by the harness from wherever the agent happens to stand, so the base directory is not ours to guess and two callers would silently read two different corpora. ⚠️ `CTXROUTE_DOCS_DIR` STILL WINS over this key: the variable is RESERVED for tests and doctor.js, and it is how every probe isolates itself in a throwaway tmpdir.

sessionDocsDir.description: ABSOLUTE path of the directory holding the SESSION DOCS corpus (docs/session/*.md, injected at every SessionStart and after every compaction) (2026-08-24). OPTIONAL: with the key ABSENT, the corpus stays exactly where it has always been, the code-derived <repo>/docs/session — zero default change. ⚠️ Same reason as `docsDir`: the address of the KNOWLEDGE must stop following the address of the ENGINE, or a frozen copy of the code freezes the maintainer's docs with it and their edits stop reaching production in silence. 🛑 A RELATIVE or otherwise invalid value is a NAMED REFUSAL naming the key and the value, never a quiet fallback. ⚠️ `CTXROUTE_SESSIONDOCS_DIR` STILL WINS over this key (RESERVED for tests and doctor.js).

host.description: The interface the daemon BINDS and the wiring POSTs to. Default 127.0.0.1. ⚠️ LOOPBACK IS THE DEFAULT FOR A REASON: this endpoint returns the fleet's private knowledge and has NO authentication - the socket IS the boundary. Moving it off the loopback exposes that knowledge to the local network, and there is no supervisor variable able to do it by accident (there is deliberately no CTXROUTE_HTTP_HOST: environment variables are INHERITED).

port.description: The port the daemon BINDS and the wiring POSTs to. Default 8787, in the IANA dynamic range. ⚠️ `CTXROUTE_HTTP_PORT` STILL WINS over this half - unlike the `CTXROUTE_*_DIR` variables it is NOT test-reserved (service/ctxroute-http.service declares it, install-windows.ps1 reads it back), and both consumers resolve through the same single point, so the escape cannot move one of them alone.

listeners.description: HOW MANY LISTENING SOCKETS THE DAEMON OPENS, starting at `port` and counting UP (2026-09-18). Default 1 - nobody pays for a problem they do not have. ⚠️ IT BUYS A WAITING ROOM, NEVER SERVICE SPEED: the accept queue is capped PER SOCKET (measured on Windows: `min(backlog,200) + 32` = 232, strictly linear at 1/2/4 sockets => 232/464/928), while the daemon stays single-threaded, so N listeners let more callers WAIT, they do not make it answer faster. Raise it when the daemon reports its peak approaching the ceiling; the other wall is a different lever (worker threads). 🛑 RAISING THE BACKLOG IS NOT AN ALTERNATIVE AND IS ALREADY MEASURED DEAD: 511, 65535 and -65535 (the literal expansion of SOMAXCONN_HINT) ALL yield a depth of 232 from this runtime, stable over 12+ runs, while the SAME call from .NET yields 700-1500 queued - Winsock honours the hint, our runtime loses it. ⚠️ N DISTINCT PORTS ON EVERY PLATFORM, deliberately: SO_REUSEPORT (Node's `reusePort`) would give one port with kernel load balancing, but it exists only on Linux/DragonFly/FreeBSD/Solaris/AIX and RAISES AN ERROR elsewhere - portable correctness first, per-OS optimisation second. ⚠️ Under SOCKET ACTIVATION the OS owns the sockets and the daemon IGNORES this key, exactly like `host` and `port`.

workers.description: ✅ WIRED 2026-09-20 - N server THREADS, each binding its OWN listening sockets and doing all the expensive work of its own requests (the nginx/HAProxy shape), with ONE owner thread holding the store and the three invocation tables and answering O(1) questions synchronously. Proven byte-identical to the single-threaded daemon by `test/thread-pool-differential.test.js`, which is the acceptance criterion - the facade, never the speed. 🛑 REFUSED WITH SOCKET ACTIVATION: serving an inherited descriptor from a worker thread is UNMEASURED on every kernel here, and an unmeasured transport is not something this daemon starts. HOW MANY THREADS SERVE THOSE SOCKETS (2026-09-19). Default 0 - NO pool at all, i.e. exactly today's behaviour byte for byte; a capability that arrives switched on changes production for people who never asked for it, which is why nginx ships `worker_processes 1` too. ⚠️ IT BUYS PARALLELISM, WHERE `listeners` BUYS A WAITING ROOM - and conflating the two is a measured mistake: a socket caps its accept queue at 232 on Windows (strictly linear, 1/2/4 -> 232/464/928) while the daemon answers on ONE loop, so sockets let more callers WAIT and threads make it ANSWER faster. Production today is four sockets on ONE thread. 🛑 THE ONE CONSTRAINT IS `workers <= listeners`: a thread with no socket has nothing to accept and would cost a V8 isolate and its heap for nothing. It is a NAMED REFUSAL, never a clamp - clamping starts a pool of a size nobody declared. 📐 `auto` follows nginx's published convention (`worker_processes number | auto`) because an adopter already knows that word, and resolves to HALF the cores capped at 8: this daemon shares its machine with the harness, the MCP servers and the agents it serves, so taking every core starves the very clients it answers. 🛑 THREADS ARE NOT THE CURE FOR `ECONNREFUSED` - those come from a slow CLIENT, established on 200 stalls where 100% of the elapsed time is the wait for the request body. Decisions and refusals live in `src/worker-pool-pure.js`; the architecture and what each remaining step must prove are in the backlog under "LA DIRECTION EXACTE DU MULTI-COEURS".

lifecycle.description: WHEN THE DAEMON RUNS (2026-09-29). Default `auto`. `on-demand`: the daemon runs only while a harness uses it - a session asks the OS supervisor to start it (Windows: Task Scheduler runs the task, a no-op when it already runs; Linux/macOS: the socket-activated unit starts it at the first connection) and it LEAVES with exit 0 once `idleSeconds` pass with no request. `login`: it stays up from login and never leaves on idle - the server shape. `auto` resolves on what a restart depends on: Linux and macOS => `on-demand` (the OS holds the socket, so an idle exit costs nothing: the next connection starts a fresh daemon); every Windows edition => `login` (nothing holds the socket, and third-party "do not disturb" modes can pause Task Scheduler - measured 2026-09-30 - so a daemon that left on idle might not come back). `on-demand` on Windows is an explicit opt-in. The resolved mode and its reason ride the daemon's `start` journal line. 🛑 The stop is by INACTIVITY, never by counting sessions: a crashed session never says goodbye, so a count lies for ever. 🛑 An unknown value is a NAMED REFUSAL at start, never a quiet `auto`. Decided in `src/lifecycle-pure.js`.

idleSeconds.description: HOW LONG AN ON-DEMAND DAEMON WAITS WITH NO REQUEST BEFORE LEAVING, in seconds (2026-09-29). Default 1800 (thirty minutes): a coffee break must not cost a cold start - and a cold start is never a loss, since every harness prompt asks the supervisor again. The window closes on EQUALITY of a shared activity counter bumped by every request of every thread, so the daemon leaves between ONE and TWO windows after its last request. Ignored in `login` mode. Out of range or not an integer => a NAMED REFUSAL at start.

http.description: THE ADDRESS THE DAEMON BINDS AND THE WIRING POSTS TO — ONE fact, ONE key, ONE place (2026-08-25). Default 127.0.0.1:8787. OPTIONAL: with the key (or either half) ABSENT the address stays 127.0.0.1:8787, byte for byte the historical behaviour. ⚠️ IT USED TO BE FOUR PLACES, TWO PER FIELD: `HOST` and `DEFAULT_PORT` constants in src/hooks/http-server.js (what the daemon binds) facing `transport.host` and `transport.port` in wiring.json (what the harness POSTs to). Each pair agreed by luck and nothing compared them — the same class as the 2026-08-22 split brain, where one truth held in nineteen hand-edited copies failed in silence. A wiring pointing where nobody listens gets ECONNREFUSED instantly, and the http lane has NO fallback: every frame of every action would be lost, with no error and no badge. 🛑 IT IS ONE GROUPED KEY AND NOT TWO SIBLINGS (`httpHost` beside `httpPort`): a listening address is ONE fact, and two settings for one fact is the same disease one level up, in the vocabulary. Both consumers read it WHOLE, in one call (`paths.httpEndpoint()`). 🛑 An invalid value is a NAMED REFUSAL naming the key and the value, never a quiet fallback: an operator who declared an address asked for that address. ⚠️ Under SOCKET ACTIVATION the OS owns the listening socket and the daemon IGNORES this key: the address is then the unit's (`ListenStream=`, `SockNodeName`/`SockServiceName`), and this key still tells the WIRING where to knock.

frames.description: NUMBER OF FRAMES declared for ONE action — the framework's BANDWIDTH (07/08/2026). Default 12. Capacity of an action = frames × (budgetInjection − envelope); measured 07/08/2026: 12 × 7,661 = 91,932 characters, for a real worst-case load of 65,265 c (71%). What overflows is NEVER lost (emission queue) but lands on the NEXT action — so the agent will have acted on partial knowledge. ⚠️ THIS KEY DRIVES NOTHING AT RUNTIME: the harness launches exactly the processes declared in ITS wiring (settings.json), cold, and no extra frame can be created during a call. It is the SOURCE OF TRUTH that `doctor.js --settings` confronts with the real wiring — two places for one number diverge silently, defect MEASURED on 05/08/2026 (a skill delivered over 11 actions instead of 1, 995 green tests). ⚠️ RAISING IT COSTS: each frame is a process launched on EVERY tool call, even empty (~330 ms measured) — 12 ⇒ ~4 s, 50 ⇒ ~17 s. Don't inflate 'just in case'; the overflow alarm says when it is justified.

afterFrames.description: NUMBER OF FRAMES declared for the moment AFTER a tool answered (23/09/2026) — the bandwidth of the docs that wait for an answer (`response`). Declared APART from `frames` and meant to stay SMALL, because the harness POSTs its WHOLE payload to every declaration, answer included: 32 frames would ship a 100 KB answer 32 times per tool call. What does not fit is never lost — it goes to the emission queue and leaves with the next action. Like `frames` it DRIVES NOTHING AT RUNTIME: it is the source of truth `tools/wiring-generate.js` writes from and `doctor.js --settings` confronts with the wiring. ABSENT OR 0 = THE MOMENT IS OFF (the default since 2026-09-23): the generator writes no declaration for it and the doctor requires none. Any other value that is not an integer >= 1 is a named refusal, so a typo never reads as off.

logging.description: JOURNALS (2026-10-04) — where ctxroute records what went wrong, and how much disk it may use. Two files under the state directory: `ctxroute-daemon.log` (the daemon's life: start, exits, stalls) and `ctxroute-hooks.log` (a hook that failed and stayed fail-open). Each rotates by size: at `maxBytes` the current file becomes `.1`, the older ones shift, and only `keptFiles` files (the current one included) survive, so the whole cost is bounded for life. ERRORS ARE ALWAYS WRITTEN, whatever the level: a failure at night with debug off still leaves its line. `debug` adds the verbose trace (one line per daemon request, each hook's decision) and is OFF by default. A change is read at the next record, without a restart. ABSENT = level `error`, 262144 bytes, 2 files — the daemon journal as it always was. A value outside the bounds is a NAMED REFUSAL: the journal says why (`logging-refused`) and runs on the defaults, never on a guess.

level.description: `error` (default): errors and the daemon's life events. `debug`: plus the verbose trace — switch it on to diagnose, off when done (it writes on every daemon request).

maxBytes.description: Size at which a journal file turns over, in bytes. Default 262144 (256 KB). Same bounds as `src/log-pure.js` BOUNDS, tied by a cell.

keptFiles.description: Files kept per journal, the current one included. Default 2. 1 = the journal starts over at each rotation. Lowering it removes the extra generations at the next rotation.

note.description: AUTHOR COMMENT — never read by the engine.

wrapUp.description: EXPERIMENTAL OPTION (2026-10-04) — when the context window approaches its wall, the agent is FORCED to write its session knowledge down (injectable docs, memory, regression tests) before it may end its turn. A sensor reports how full the context is (Claude Code: the mod `mods/wrap-up-sensor`, event `session.measure`); at each end of turn above `atPercent`, the `Stop` hook refuses to let the agent stop until the JUDGES declared for the project pass, at most `maxNudges` times. It NEVER blocks a compaction (a blocked compaction hands the session to a human). OFF unless `enabled: true`; switched off, the generated wiring is byte-identical. Codex is not supported: no hook input carries the context fill.

enabled.description: The switch. Absent or false = the option does not exist: nothing is wired, nothing is written.

atPercent.description: Fill (percent of the context window) from which the end of turn is judged. Keep it BELOW the harness compaction point, so the agent writes while it still remembers. Default 70.

maxNudges.description: How many times the end of turn may be refused in one context window. The bound IS the anti-loop: past it the session is released, loudly. Default 3.

judgeTimeoutSeconds.description: Time bound of ONE judge run, in seconds (judges run in parallel). A judge that overruns is stopped with its whole process tree and never holds the session. Ceiling 540, below the 600 s the wiring declares on the hook. Default 120.

message.description: The text handed to the agent with a refusal, in ANY language. `{percent}` is replaced by the fill. Absent = the default English message. Exclusive with `messageFile`.

messageFile.description: Same as `message`, read from a file (resolved next to this config file). Unreadable = the default message, and the human is told.

judges.description: The adopter's judges, by name. A judge is ANY command (a script, a suite of judges, a call to a model): it receives a versioned JSON on stdin (`version`, `sessionId`, `cwd`, `context`, `atPercent`, `nudges`), exits 0 when the work is done, anything else when it is not — its stdout (raw text, or `{ "ok": false, "findings": [{ "file", "message", "severity" }] }`) is handed to the agent. Its PERIMETER is declared with the SAME words as a skill, matched on the session cwd; every judge whose perimeter covers the session runs. No judge for a project = one nudge with the message, then the context is settled.

command.description: The judge as an ARGUMENT VECTOR, run WITHOUT a shell in the session cwd: the program, then its arguments (e.g. ["node", "scripts/check-docs.js"]). No shell on purpose: the system shell differs per OS (cmd on Windows, /bin/sh elsewhere), so a command line would behave differently on the three systems.

filterMode.description: GLOBAL PER-TARGET FILTER (generalized 15/08/2026, work item 52 — it used to target MCP servers only: class ㊴). whitelist = the framework only injects on actions whose target is in filterList. blacklist = never on those targets ('NEVER inject on our production tools'). An excluded target still counts as 'foreign' for the other docs' counters. SINGLE application point = gate.js, exclusion OBSERVABLE (badge + explain.js). Also tunable PER CATEGORY via defaults.{source}.filterMode — a `"none"` declared there UNSUBSCRIBES the category from a global filter.

filterList.description: TARGETS of the filterMode: MCP SERVER name ("stripe" — historical semantics), exact TOOL name ("Bash", "mcp__stripe__pay"), or wildcard "*" (52, 15/08/2026). The filterMode+filterList pair cascades TOGETHER: the stage that provides the mode provides its list.

servers.description: STRUCTURAL per-server settings (routing), NEVER cadence: per-doc mode/threshold = the doc's frontmatter (keys removed from the schema 17/07/2026, zero duplication).

subToolParam.description: Dotted path of the param carrying the real operation of a single-tool proxy MCP (e.g. "args.tool" for Odoo) — enables level 3, docs/mcp/{server}/{subTool}.md.

skillsWithoutPerimeter.description: SKILLS DELIBERATELY WITHOUT A PERIMETER + SWITCH of the zero-silence discipline (19/07/2026 — mirror of `inject: never`). EXPLICIT OPT-IN: the presence of THIS key (even []) activates the reverse direction of skill-registry-gate; absent = no exhaustiveness required (using `skills` imposes NOTHING — a language never imposes a policy). Every harness skill MUST be EITHER registered in `skills` (auto-injection by perimeter) OR listed HERE (reference/on-demand, manual invocation). A skill in NEITHER list = RED (skill-registry-gate, reverse direction) — a FORGOTTEN perimeter and a deliberately silent skill are indistinguishable without this declaration.

defaults.description: PER-SOURCE DEFAULTS — 3rd stage of the cascade (04/08/2026). Generalizes the old `skillDefaults`, which offered that stage only to skills: between the global ('the whole corpus') and the entry ('this very doc'), 'all docs of THIS category' was missing. Full cascade, 4 stages: entry (frontmatter/registry) > defaults.{source} > global (mode/defaultThreshold/defaultDriftUnit) > FRAMEWORK default. TOTAL fallback at every stage: absent key or invalid value ⇒ we go down, never an error. EVERYTHING is optional — `defaults` absent = previous behavior, identical. ⚠️ DELIBERATE ASYMMETRY, do not 'fix' it: the `skill` source does NOT consult the global (its framework default is `once`, the docs' is `smart`) — a skill is project knowledge, a doc is an action reminder. Making them uniform would change the behavior of all skills the moment a global config is set. ⚠️ `session` (2026-10-07) carries ONLY `category`: docs/session/ docs are delivered by session-inject.js once to each context that starts (main session AND sub-agents), consulting no cadence — so `mode`/`threshold`/`driftUnit`/`enforce`/`response` would be ACCEPTED and INERT there (the false green this repo killed on 31/07) and are refused by its own definition. It said 'NO session key' until `category` reached that corpus: a word missing from one corpus is a hole in the language. The keys admitted here are the `id`s of the source-adapters.js registry plus `session` — sealed by a gate.

file.description: Default for docs triggered by PATH (frontmatter match/rules).

skill.description: Default for perimeter skills (ex-`skillDefaults`, same semantics).

tool.description: Default for docs triggered by a native TOOL NAME (frontmatter tool:).

session.description: Default for docs/session/ docs, delivered once to each context when it starts — the main agent's session AND every sub-agent (2026-10-07). ONLY `category` means something there (e.g. `["role:main"]` keeps the whole folder away from sub-agents unless a doc says otherwise): a session doc has no cadence, nothing to refuse and no tool answer, so every other key is refused here, never accepted and inert.

skills.description: Registry of skills triggered by PERIMETER (18/07/2026). GLOBAL config that the framework OWNS — never inside the skill file itself (harness property, unmastered format, fragile to updates: doctrine 'frontmatter only in what we control 100%'). Key = skill name (= the harness's {key}.md skill file, sealed by skill-registry-gate). Injects the skill's BODY read live (single source — pointer fallback if unreadable). Matching = the SAME as the file source (matchingDocs reused), SAME vocabulary as the docs: match/scope/exclude.

anyOf.description: BARE WILDCARD FORBIDDEN (EXACT parity with frontmatter.validate): `tool: ["*"]` without `scope` or `exclude` would inject the WHOLE skill on EVERY tool call. The wildcard exists to say 'whatever the tool, WHEN this' — the WHEN is mandatory.

rules.description: PER-ENTRY FORM (19/07/2026, doc parity): DIFFERENT conditions per pattern — [{"pattern":"deploy.sh","scope":["project-a"]},{"pattern":"clients"}]. Replaces match/scope/exclude (mixing them = a contradiction, two truths = drift). A homogeneous skill keeps the simple match/scope/exclude format.

scope.description: FLAT FORM = OR (inherited, untouched) - GROUPED FORM = AND of ORs (㊺①, 14/08/2026): [["a"],["b"]] = a AND b, [["a","b"],["c"]] = (a OR b) AND c. EXACT MIRROR of frontmatter.js::formeScopeErreur - two form declarations that diverge = class ㊴, invisible to a gate that probes the PRESENCE of a key. 🛑 MIXED forms REFUSED (oneOf): the danger of this extension is AMBIGUITY, not the limit - an author writing ["a","b"] meaning AND gets an OR, hence a WIDER rule, SILENTLY.

keys.description: WHICH parameter keys this entry may see. Flat list = the same universe for the three axes; object = one universe PER axis (match/scope/exclude). A name prefixed with '-' REMOVES the key from the default universe (blacklist); without the prefix the list REPLACES it (whitelist), which is what allows an entry to read a key the harness profile never declared. MIXED forms are ADMITTED and mean ADJUST: at least one '-' present => the default universe minus the removals plus the bare names; no '-' at all => the list REPLACES the universe. Refusing the mixed form (until 2026-08-20) left 'the default plus this one key' writable only as a hand-made enumeration of the whole universe, which stops following the profile the day it gains a key. MIRROR of frontmatter.validate — the two declarations must not diverge (class 34: a gate probing a key's PRESENCE never sees its FORM).

match.description: FILE DIMENSION — substring patterns (same rules as file match): when a tool param contains one, the skill injects. Pick strings DISTINCTIVE of the project (over-genericity = over-injection).

servers.description: MCP DIMENSION, 3 GRAINS (18/07/2026, same levels as MCP docs): "infra" = any tool of the server · "mailer/send_mail" = THAT precise tool (suffix of mcp__{server}__{tool}) · "odoo/create_invoice" = THAT sub-tool (via servers.{server}.subToolParam). Lib primitives reused (serverName/toolSuffix/getByPath — zero new matching). A project is worked through files AND through MCP — the 2 dimensions are a UNION.

tool.description: TOOL DIMENSION (㊴, 12/08/2026) — EXACT tool name (===, never a substring) + wildcard "*". SAME word, SAME meaning as the docs' frontmatter `tool:`: no vocabulary created, we extend the usage to a source that lacked it. This is what finally lets a skill react to an ACTION (with `scope`, which sees ALL params) and not only to a PLACE. A skill could NOT react to a parameter's CONTENT: real measured cost = a client email drafted without its folder.

mode.description: Cadence (default once). Skills = a NEW source with no legacy parity → once/smart FREE from day one (unlike file docs, held at dumb until the Codex port).

threshold.description: The N of smart mode for this skill.

driftUnit.description: Unit of the smart counter for THIS skill: tool (tool calls) or turn (conversation turns). Last word of the cascade.

enforce.description: REFUSE the action instead of informing (05/08/2026) — SAME word, SAME meaning as the docs' frontmatter (anti-synonym law). ⚠️ Only effective with an EFFECTIVE `once` mode (skills' framework default): gate.js NEVER honors `enforce` on `dumb`/`smart`, otherwise the blocked agent retries and gets re-blocked ENDLESSLY. An explicit `false` CANCELS the `defaults.skill` inheritance.

category.description: WHO receives this SKILL — SAME word, SAME meaning as the docs' frontmatter `category` (anti-synonym law): declared categories plus the derived identity (`role:main`, `role:subagent`, `type:<agent type>`), flat = OR, grouped = AND, `-` subtracts. Absent = every context sees it (unchanged, generalist skill).

response.description: Deliver this SKILL only AFTER the tool answered, and only on answers its `scope`/`exclude` accept — SAME word, SAME meaning as the docs' frontmatter `response` (anti-synonym law). Absent = decided before the action (unchanged).

note.description: AUTHOR COMMENT (04/08/2026) — the ONLY field the engine NEVER reads. Addressee = whoever comes to MODIFY this entry ('why this mode', 'why this scope', 're-check after such version'), not the agent that acts. Exact mirror of the docs' frontmatter `note` key: one concept = one word, whatever the corpus. 🛑 BOUND: NEVER the why of an INVARIANT — that one stays in the body, visible to the acting agent; an invariant deprived of its reason drifts.

exclude.description: Patterns to reject (matched on the current path/command) — homonyms (node_modules, dist...).
